Oyo State Governor, Seyi Makinde, has declared that he will seek only a four-year presidential term if elected in 2027, arguing that Southern Nigeria should complete its eight-year turn in the presidency by 2031. Makinde, who is contesting the presidential ticket on the platform of Allied People’s Movement, said he was entering the contest to win and would not seek a second term, linking his position to what he described as fairness, national unity and respect for the country’s political understanding on power rotation. The governor also said his proposed administration would prioritise security, employment, enterprise development and stronger public institutions under his Reset Agenda. His campaign office, in a statement on Sunday, said Makinde believed the South should be allowed to complete the remaining four years of its eight-year presidential tenure before power returned to the North in 2031. “His commitment to a single four-year term is rooted in his belief that national unity rests on fairness, mutual respect and fidelity to the understandings that hold our federation together. The governor’s position makes a one-term presidency a central part of his pitch to Nigerians as political manoeuvring intensifies ahead of the next general election. The campaign office said the proposed four years would be tied to specific governance priorities rather than an extended stay in office. 2027: Ex-minister Akinjide backs Tinubu, Alli Sultan urges Muslims to champion national unity, religious tolerance UPDATED: Olubadan hosts Emir Sanusi, warns against politicising traditional institutions “Those four years must count in the lives of Nigerians. His priorities are to restore security, expand opportunities for enterprise and employment, strengthen public institutions and give families confidence in their future. He is seeking a mandate tied to clear priorities and measurable results,” it added. The statement also said Makinde had been engaging political leaders and Nigerians across different social groups as part of efforts to build support for his presidential ambition. It described the engagements as part of his attempt to secure the political backing required to win the election and govern effectively. “Makinde is in this contest to earn the people’s trust, win their votes and serve as President for one purposeful four-year term,” the campaign office stated. It added that his Reset Agenda would guide his campaign and that the governor was taking his message to citizens across the country. Ayoola Babalola
